task_text: A developer edits a source file in the checkout after RepoSourceEvidence was published. A later FACT validation is reported as either returning the old committed bytes or raising repository_source_mismatch. Diagnose the exact authority path, distinguish a dirty worktree from a real committed-source mismatch, identify the smallest safe regression test and remediation, and do not edit the repository.

evidence_universe.role: immutable ContentRef and accepted binding store

must_see_ground_truth.requirement: M2a read_bytes/read_text are tied to the exact committed Git object database, not the mutable checkout filesystem.
A dirty worktree after view creation must not change bytes returned by that exact view; a newer commit is a different RepoView basis.
repository_source_mismatch means the committed entry/object or accepted immutable bytes do not equal; it is not the expected signal for an ordinary dirty checkout.
The safe regression test must compare committed bytes and accepted raw bytes before/after a worktree edit and separately exercise fabricated or stale evidence.

known_constraints: never read mutable worktree bytes as authority
same exact RepoView required for source validation
no retry or repair side effects
Legacy and runtime are out of scope
known_unknowns: The report does not identify whether the observed mismatch came from a newer RepoView, fabricated M2b bytes, or a wrong repository; the answer must keep those hypotheses separate.

source_inference_distinctions.statement: Dirty checkout content is an observation about the worktree, not exact committed source authority.
An error code alone cannot prove which mismatch branch occurred without the bound view/object evidence.
